| $y$ | $0$ | $a$ | $b$ | $18$ |

e-9211.knowledge_point: Finding Distributions of Squared Random Variables: Many-to-One Transformations
e-9211.problem:
The random variable $X$ has the following probability distribution.

| $x$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f_X(x)$ | $0.2$ | $0.1$ | $0.3$ | $0.3$ | $0.1$ |

Let $Y=1-X^2.$ The distribution of $Y$ is given below.

| $y$ | $a$ | $b$ | $1$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f_Y(y)$ | $0.3$ | $c$ | $d$ |

Find the values of $a,b,c,$ and $d.$
e-9211.worked_solution:
First, let's add a $Y = 1-X^2$ row to our table.

| $x$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ | $2$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $-3$ | $0$ | $1$ | $0$ | $-3$ |
| $f_X(x)$ | ${\color{red}{0.2}}$ | ${\color{blue}{0.1}}$ | $0.3$ | ${\color{blue}{0.3}}$ | ${\color{red}{0.1}}$ |

From the table, we see that $Y \in \{-3,0,1\}.$ Notice that we now have two columns for both $Y=-3$ and $Y=0.$

We calculate the probabilities associated with each value of $Y$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y=-3) & =0.2+0.1 \\ P(Y=0) & =0.1+0.3 \\ P(Y=1) & =0.3\end{aligned}
$$

This gives the following table:

| $y$ | $-3$ | $0$ | $1$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f_Y(y)$ | $0.3$ | $0.4$ | $0.3$ |

e-9177.knowledge_point: Calculating a Probability Involving a Squared Random Variable
e-9177.problem:
The random variable $X$ has the following probability distribution.

| $x$ | $-4$ | $-2$ | $0$ | $2$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $f(x)$ | $0.3$ | $0.2$ | $0.1$ | $0.1$ | $0.3$ |

Calculate $P(X^2 = 4).$
e-9177.worked_solution:
Let's first add an $X^2$ row to our table.

| $x$ | $-4$ | $-2$ | $0$ | $2$ | $4$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $x^2$ | $16$ | $4$ | $0$ | $4$ | $16$ |
| $f(x)$ | $0.3$ | $0.2$ | $0.1$ | $0.1$ | $0.3$ |

From the second and third rows of our table, we can immediately conclude that 

$$
P(X^2 = 4) = 0.2+0.1 = 0.3.
$$

| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| ${f}_{Y}(y)$ | $0.3$ | $c$ | $0.1$ |

after.worked_solution:

| $x$ | $-2$ | $-1$ | $0$ | $1$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $y$ | $4$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ | $0$ | $\frac{1}{4}$ |

$$
\begin{aligned}P(Y=0) & =0.3 \\ P(Y=\frac{1}{4}) & =0.2+0.4 \\ P(Y=4) & =0.1\end{aligned}
